body: Note: I have added a method to get `AdvancedColorInfo` as a Godot Dictionary, but not sure if it's needed for something.

This introduces C++ exceptions whereas we didn't use any before, is it an issue? Typically, we want to avoid them due to the added binary size (and performance issues in hot paths).

Searching in the codebase, I noticed there are two uses of `try {} catch {}` in `drivers/metal` as well. There are several in third-party code, but they all appear to be disabled at compile-time through `#ifdef`s.

WinRT headers internally depends on exceptions, so it is enabled specifically for this few files, same for Metal.

Also, both are C++20.
I wonder if there's a significant binary size impact of having some exception handling code just for WinRT and Metal.
I'll check size with and without WinRT enabled in a moment. We can get rid of this specific block, but changing in the headers is not feasible, it used a lot.

Entire WinRT part of the code (this PR, emoji picker, OneCore TTS) adds about 64 KB in both debug editor build, and release template with LTO.

Changing this specific block to non-throwing variant seems to have no effect.

> Changing this specific block to non-throwing variant seems to have no effect.

I might be misunderstanding something here… the code has not changed and still has the `try catch`. Was this supposed to be changed? (Specifically changed to use the non-throwing variant so that the try catch aren’t needed anymore?)

> Was this supposed to be changed?

No, I have checked it locally, but did not change the PR since there's no difference.
